Resolves #18006

Related: #18004

The dock shape gate now rejects an `edge-zone` whose `zones` container is not a JSON record, instead of collapsing malformed input into the legitimate empty `e{}` shape and letting `TopologyDiff` fabricate error-free semantic categories.

Evidence: L2 (pure data-plane unit and mutation evidence) → L2 required (AC-1–7). No residuals.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `DockTopologyDiff.spec.mjs` covers string, array, `null`, and number containers; each produces gate errors and a null fingerprint. |
| AC-2 | The same arm proves a well-formed empty `{}` zones record remains clean with shape `e{}`. |
| AC-3 | Every malformed form is exercised as both `before` and `after`; each error keeps the existing side-named prefix. |
| AC-4 | One property assertion binds `Document.validate()` rejection to fingerprint-gate rejection for every specimen. |
| AC-5 | Every semantic category is asserted empty, preventing the former fabricated-removes result. |
| AC-6 | Red-first control on unchanged `dev`: focused suite was 8/9, failing at validator/gate disagreement; restored source is 9/9. |
| AC-7 | Full unit corpus: 2,927/2,927. |

## Deltas from ticket

The diagnostic stays in the fingerprint walk's existing voice. No traversal unification, broad container census, or `Document.validate()` change was needed.

## Test Evidence

- Pre-fix focused control: 8 passed, 1 failed at the new validator/gate property.
- Post-fix focused suite: 9/9 passed.
- Full unit suite: 2,927/2,927 passed.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge I raised and then resolved against myself — the one thing in this diff that changes behaviour beyond the ticket's literal wording.**

AC-1 scopes the fix to `zones` **present but not a record**. The old code was `node.zones || {}`, so an edge-zone with `zones` **absent** fingerprinted clean as `e{}`. `isJsonRecord(undefined)` is `false`, so absent `zones` now fails closed too. That is strictly wider than the AC, and my first read had it as a possible regression against AC-7 (*"no existing fixture that currently fingerprints clean starts erroring"*).

It is not a regression, and the reason is the point of the ticket. `validate()` at `Document.mjs:799` and the schema walk at `:399` both already reject absent `zones` with the **same** `isJsonRecord` call. So an edge-zone without `zones` was **already invalid**; the fingerprint walk was the single path that disagreed, by coercing. Widening to match is precisely AC-4's biconditional, not a scope overrun — and reusing the predicate instead of writing a new one is what makes the agreement structural rather than coincidental.

**Also examined, no concern found:** whether the biconditional arm can pass vacuously. `expect(validationErrors.length > 0).toBe(gate.errors.length > 0)` is satisfied by both sides being false — but the arm separately asserts `gate.fingerprint === null` for every specimen, which pins the gate side true, so the biconditional cannot be satisfied by mutual silence. Non-vacuous by construction.

**Non-blocking observation.** The specimen list is `['main-split', [], null, 42]`. `undefined` is not among them, yet it is now a fail-closed form and it is the one an omitted key actually produces in practice. AC-1's "at minimum" is met, so this is not an action — but a fifth specimen would cost one array entry and would pin the case I spent most of this review chasing. Your call.
